entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-9583-h5hc-x8cw: React Router has Path Traversal in File Session Storage
entry.content:
React Router has Path Traversal in File Session Storage

Aliases: CVE-2025-61686

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • @react-router/node — fixed in 7.9.4
  • @remix-run/node — fixed in 2.17.2
  • @remix-run/deno — fixed in 2.17.2

If applications use `createFileSessionStorage()` from `@react-router/node` (or `@remix-run/node`/`@remix-run/deno` in Remix v2) with an [**unsigned cookie**](https://reactrouter.com/explanation/sessions-and-cookies#signing-cookies), it is possible for an attacker to cause the session to try to read/write from a location outside the specified session file directory. The success of the attack would depend on the permissions of the web server process to access those files. Read files cannot be returned directly to the attacker. Session file reads would only succeed if the file matched the expected session file format. If the file matched the session file format, the data would be populated into the server side session but not directly returned to the attacker unless the application logic r…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-c9cv-mq2m-ppp3: Nuxt: URL-handling weaknesses in `navigateTo` and `reloadNuxtApp`: SSR open redirect, client-side script execution via the `open` option, and protocol-relative bypass in `reloadNuxtApp`

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-3753-m2x2-q623: File Viewer: DOM XSS via unsafe hyperlink schemes in the legacy DOC renderer
entry.content:
File Viewer: DOM XSS via unsafe hyperlink schemes in the legacy DOC renderer

Aliases: CVE-2026-91127

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • @file-viewer/doc — fixed in 2.3.1
  • msdoc-viewer — fixed in 0.2.2

### Summary Before 2.3.1, the legacy `.doc` renderer emitted document hyperlink targets after HTML escaping but without a URL-scheme allowlist. A crafted `.doc` could therefore render a live `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:`, or similarly unsafe link. Script could execute in the embedding origin if a viewer clicked it. ### Impact Applications rendering untrusted legacy `.doc` files with `@file-viewer/doc` or the `msdoc-viewer` compatibility package could expose their origin to attacker-controlled script after link interaction. ### Fix Version 2.3.1 centralizes link handling, removes control-character and scheme confusion, blocks external document links by default, and in explicit allow mode accepts only HTTP(S), mail, telephone, safe relative URLs, and internal bookmarks. The render…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-7q85-xj36-vmfc: adm-zip: Uncontrolled memory allocation via the declared uncompressed size (DoS)
entry.content:
adm-zip: Uncontrolled memory allocation via the declared uncompressed size (DoS)

Aliases: CVE-2026-77301

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • adm-zip — fixed in 0.6.1

### Summary adm-zip allocates an entry's output buffer from the declared uncompressed size (central-directory `size` field) before validating it against the actual data. A tiny crafted ZIP that declares a huge uncompressed size forces a multi-gigabyte allocation from a few bytes. ### Impact On adm-zip 0.5.17 (latest), Node 24, a 105-byte ZIP with one stored entry declaring size = 1,774,399,200 makes `new AdmZip(buf).getEntries()[0].getData()` commit ~1.8 GB of resident memory in ~4.4 s before throwing `Error: ADM-ZIP: CRC32 checksum failed`, roughly 16 million times the input size. Because the buffer is committed before any validation, on a memory-constrained host (containers, serverless, small VMs) the allocation OOM-kills the process before the CRC check (uncatchable), and concurrent re…
